study_identification_part.si_4_title: Investigating dopaminergic abnormalities in schizophrenia and /uniFB01 rst-episode psychosis with normative modelling and multisite molecular neuroimaging

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Bayesian linear regression for voxel-wise normative models using PCNToolkit.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: After data harmonisation, Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) was used to estimate voxel-wise NMs (i.e., one model per grey matter voxel) of dopamine receptor density and dopamine synthesis capacity from [ 11 C]-( + )-PHNO and [ 18 F]FDOPA data of the HC samples.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Non-displaceable binding potential (BPND) for [11C]-(+)-PHNO and Ki_cer for [18F]FDOPA dopamine synthesis capacity.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: dopamine D2/3 receptor density was measured using non-displaceable binding potential (BPND [49]) as the parameter of interest. Dopamine synthesis capacity indicated by the parameter Ki cer (sometimes indicated as Ki, min -1 ) was quanti /uniFB01 ed with the Gjedde-Patlak graphical method using the cerebellum as the reference region.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age, sex, and BMI for [11C]-(+)-PHNO; age and sex for [18F]FDOPA.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: the selected independent variables were sex, age, and BMI for [ 11 C]-( + )-PHNO, and age and sex for [ 18 F]FDOPA.
